stem: Which number does not belong to this group: 4, 9, 16, 25, 35, 49?

per_option_rationale.rationale: 4, 9, 16, 25, 49 are perfect squares (2², 3², 4², 5², 7²). 35 is not a perfect square.
Student picks 16 after misidentifying the rule as odd squares only, ignoring even perfect squares.
Student picks 25 by trying a gap-based rule and finding differences irregular, missing the perfect-square pattern.
Student picks 49 after incorrectly checking 7 as composite, not recognising 7² = 49 is still a perfect square.

explanation: All members except 35 are perfect squares: 4=2², 9=3², 16=4², 25=5², 49=7². 35=5×7 is not a perfect square, so 35 is the odd one out.

explanation_sections.punchline: Every number in the group is a perfect square except 35. 35 = 5 × 7 has no integer square root, so it does not belong.
explanation_sections.approach: For odd-one-out number questions, test a single defining property across all members. Try: perfect squares, perfect cubes, primes, multiples of a fixed number. Write the root or factor of each number beside it. The one that fails the property is the answer.
explanation_sections.lesson: Not every odd number is a non-square, and not every large number is a non-square. Check each candidate against the integer square root, not just parity or size.
explanation_sections.timing: About 60 seconds. Computing square roots for each of the six numbers takes roughly 30 seconds. Confirm 35 is not a perfect square in under 10 seconds: 5² = 25, 6² = 36, so 35 falls between two squares.
